solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A peer turned to Conservative blue peerage

indicators.note: turned means the word for a peer is read backwards here

parts.note: a sir, a titled man, loosely stands for a peer
blue jokes are racy, risqué

explanation.surface: A lord switching his allegiance to the Tories, true-blue members of the peerage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' reverses SIR to RIS. 'Blue' looks like the Conservative colour but means risqué, RACY.
explanation.definitionFit: The peerage is the nobility as a body, the class of titled nobles.

clue.text: Acrimony controlled company, then game's up

parts.note: to run a firm is to control it, so controlled gives ran

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters for the game are read bottom to top

parts.note: RU is Rugby Union, the game

explanation.surface: Bitterness follows after a firm was run and its game was up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses RU (Rugby Union) to UR in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name deep-seated bitterness or resentment between people; they are synonyms.

clue.text: 'Protect and Serve' initially confused witness

indicators.note: confused tells us the letters of the slogan word plus initials are jumbled
initially takes the opening letters of and and Serve

explanation.surface: A police motto, 'Protect and Serve', baffles a bystander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' gives A and S from 'and Serve'; 'confused' shuffles PROTECT with them.
explanation.definitionFit: An onlooker who watches an event is both a witness and a spectator.

clue.text: Due to win, goal's included

indicators.note: included says the answer is contained within the run of letters of to win, goal's

explanation.surface: A team is due to win, with a goal counted in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Due to' reads as one phrase, but 'Due' alone is the definition; the answer sits across 'to win, goal's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Money that is due has not yet been paid, still outstanding.

clue.text: Disease caught from insects

indicators.note: from here means taken away from, so the letter for caught is removed

parts.note: crickets are chirping insects
C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An illness picked up from bugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught from' means C taken from CRICKETS. The surface suggests infection, not subtraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A childhood bone-softening condition caused by lack of vitamin D, a named illness.

clue.text: Completely love fabulous bird lifting part of bloomers

indicators.note: lifting in a down clue sends the whole string upward, read backwards

parts.note: all means wholly, completely
love is nil in tennis, the letter O
the roc is a giant mythical bird from the Arabian Nights

explanation.surface: A mythical bird hoists someone's underwear, absolutely adored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifting' reverses ALL + O + ROC. 'Bloomers' are flowers, not knickers.
explanation.definitionFit: The ring of petals in a flower is one part of a blossoming plant.

clue.text: Supporter of all things wicked?

parts.note: looks like a backer of evil, but means a holder for things with wicks, namely candles

explanation.surface: Someone who champions every kind of villainy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' is read as 'having wicks': a branched holder supports candles.
explanation.definitionFit: A branched stand holding several candles, each of which has a wick.

clue.text: Creator who made light of his work

definitions.text: Creator who made light of his work

parts.words: Creator who made light of his work
parts.note: making light of something usually means dismissing it; here the inventor literally made light, the incandescent bulb

explanation.surface: A modest maker who played down his achievements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made light of' is taken literally: the American inventor is credited with the practical light bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas, the prolific American inventor, developed a practical electric bulb.

clue.text: Slow movement of stake gripping desperate character

indicators.note: gripping means the stake word holds the character's name inside it

parts.note: an ante is a poker stake put up before the deal
Desperate Dan is a strongman from the British comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: A slowing of play as a gambler clutches a frantic man.
explanation.walkthrough: Desperate Dan is a cartoon strongman in Britain's Dandy comic.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical marking for a moderately slow tempo, often naming a slow section of a symphony.

clue.text: Provokes through obscenity, almost

parts.note: in can mean by way of, as in 'in writing', so through gives in

indicators.note: almost means the word for obscenity loses its last letter

parts.note: a curse is a swear word, an obscenity

explanation.surface: Someone causes offence by nearly swearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final E of CURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To bring trouble or anger on oneself is to provoke it, to bring it about.

clue.text: Endlessly frightened before opening question

indicators.note: endlessly means the phrase for frightened loses its final letter

parts.note: frightened is 'in terror'
a gate is an opening in a fence or wall

explanation.surface: A terrified person, before the start, asks something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' cuts the last R from IN TERROR, then GATE follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To grill a suspect is to question them closely and at length.

clue.text: Play endless record by Queen in can

indicators.note: endless means the word for record loses its last letter

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: in means the queen's letter goes inside the can

parts.note: a pot is a container, a can
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A broken record playing beside the Queen in the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' gives DIS from DISC; 'in' puts R (Regina) into POT. 'Can' is slang for toilet in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To frolic or amuse oneself is to play; both are verbs for romping.

clue.text: Bug Russian government losing head for good

indicators.note: losing head for means the first letter is swapped for the letter for good

parts.note: the Kremlin is the seat of Russian government

explanation.surface: Bugging by the Russian state, losing its leader for the greater good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head for' replaces the K of KREMLIN with G.
explanation.definitionFit: An imaginary mischievous sprite blamed for faults in machines, hence a glitch or bug.

clue.text: Old transport company has single passenger vehicle

indicators.note: has means the railway initials hold the single figure within them

parts.note: LNER was the London and North Eastern Railway, a pre-nationalisation British railway
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A defunct transport firm runs a single passenger vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: LNER, the London and North Eastern Railway, was one of Britain's big four railway companies before 1948; 'has' puts I inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A large ship carrying passengers on a regular route, such as an ocean ship.

clue.text: Decipher stone tablet after time passed

indicators.note: after means the stone tablet comes after the time and passed pieces

parts.note: ran means went by, passed
a slate is a stone tablet for writing on

explanation.surface: Reading an inscribed stone after a long time has gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: To render a foreign text into plain language is to decipher its meaning.

clue.text: Provokes cricketers holding England following superb runs

indicators.note: following means the cricketers piece comes after the superb runs

parts.note: ace means excellent, superb
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

indicators.note: holding means the cricketers word contains the letter for England

parts.note: bats are batsmen, cricketers

explanation.surface: England's batsmen irritate the opposition by scoring superb runs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' and 'following' are both indicators here, one for the container and one for order.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something worse or irritate someone is to provoke; the words are synonyms.

clue.text: Bar supporter, one's moved towards end

indicators.note: moved towards end means the letter for one is shifted further along the word

parts.note: a brassiere supports, a bra
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's is 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A bar's backer has relocated to the far end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved towards end' shifts the I of BRASSIERE three places to the right.
explanation.definitionFit: A French-style café-restaurant serving drinks and simple food is a kind of bar.

clue.text: Don't make one cross?

parts.note: sounds like avoiding annoying someone, but means not marking a cross on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A plea not to anger anybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' is the mark a voter makes; someone who declines to vote makes none.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain from casting a vote at an election or meeting.

clue.text: Fires up lacking energy and strength

indicators.note: lacking means the energy letter is dropped
up in a down clue means the word for fires is read backwards

parts.note: fires, as in fires up, means animates, enlivens
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Something fires you up when energy and strength are missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses ANIMATES to SETAMINA; 'lacking' removes its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance or staying power, the ability to keep going, a kind of strength.

clue.text: Hop, skip and jump

definitions.meaning: a hop is a little leap
to skip is to bound lightly
a jump is a leap or bound

explanation.surface: The triple-jump sequence of athletics.
explanation.definitionFit: A frisky playful leap, a frolic, is synonymous with each of these springy movements.

clue.text: Tea with Hatter's companion sharing a cup

indicators.note: sharing a means the two words overlap on one letter A, so one copy goes

parts.note: cha is slang for tea
Alice shares the Mad Hatter's tea party in Alice in Wonderland

explanation.surface: The Mad Hatter and Alice share a teacup.
explanation.walkthrough: CHA and ALICE overlap on a shared A. Cha (or char) is British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblet, especially the wine cup used at Communion, is a cup.

clue.text: Minister's corporeal training about divinity with holy man

definitions.note: the 's is 'is': the minister is what the wordplay builds

indicators.note: about means the training letters surround the divinity letters

parts.note: PE is physical education
RI is religious instruction, school divinity
ST is saint, a holy man

explanation.surface: A clergyman's school PE lesson about scripture with a holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: PE (physical education) and RI (religious instruction) are British school subject abbreviations; 'Minister's' means minister is.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman ordained to serve a congregation is a minister of religion.

clue.text: Vulgar slapper after drink, first to finish

indicators.note: after means the slapper word comes after the drink
first to finish means the opening letter of the drink word goes to its end

parts.note: to sup is to drink
slapper is British slang for a promiscuous woman, a tart

explanation.surface: A crude floozy after a drink, the first to finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first to finish' moves the S of SUP to the end, UPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing a social climber, newly risen and brash, hence crude or vulgar in manner.

clue.text: Threepenny bits, occasionally wooden

indicators.note: bits, occasionally means taking every other letter of threepenny

explanation.surface: Old threepenny coins, sometimes made of wood.
explanation.walkthrough: Threepenny bits were small pre-decimal British coins.
explanation.definitionFit: An old adjective meaning made of wood, used of turned household objects.

clue.text: Look North?

definitions.meaning: one's mien or demeanour, the way one looks and carries oneself
north is a compass direction, zero degrees on the compass

explanation.definitionFit: Demeanour is a person's carriage; a compass direction is also measured in degrees.

clue.text: One may fetch stick keeping cool

indicators.note: keeping means the stick word holds the cool word inside

parts.note: a cane is a walking stick
in means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: A dog fetching a stick on a hot day keeps its cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' seems to be what is fetched, but it belongs to the wordplay; the definition is 'One may fetch'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog, the classic animal that retrieves thrown things, is a member of the dog family.

clue.text: Classy pair seen on some women

definitions.text: Classy pair seen on some women

parts.words: Classy pair seen on some women
parts.note: a smart matching pair of garments, cardigan and jumper, worn by women

explanation.surface: An elegant couple spotted on the arms of some ladies.
explanation.walkthrough: The pair is a matching jumper and cardigan worn together, a classic British women's outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: A matching cardigan and sweater sold and worn together by women.

clue.text: Go around Romeo in nude, strangely naked

indicators.note: in means the go-around-Romeo piece sits inside the shuffled nude
strangely says the letters of nude are rearranged
around means the word for go wraps the Romeo letter

parts.note: to vanish is to go, disappear
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Romeo in the nude, oddly bare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' makes UNED from NUDE, split around the inner piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Unvarnished truth is plain and bare, figuratively naked, without embellishment.
